canonical_caption: State v. Christensen (State of Tennessee v. James Robert Christensen, Jr.)
context_note: Holding matches. Under the totality of the circumstances, 'No Trespassing' signs posted near an unobstructed driveway were not sufficient to revoke the implied knock-and-talk license; Carloss (10th Cir.) cited as comparative authority reaching the same result. Directly re-verified; all keys (517 S.W.3d 60, Tenn., Apr. 7 2017, docket) confirmed.

canonical_caption: State v. Weaver (State of Texas v. Roy Andrew Weaver)
context_note: Keys REAL and correct. PROPOSITION-FRAMING CAUTION (flag for orchestrator): directly re-verified that the operative holding is SCOPE-OF-CONSENT — four officers came to Weaver's welding shop looking for a fugitive ('Bear') with his oral consent, but the search of a van backed into the loading dock exceeded that consent (his unequivocal refusal ended the license), so suppression was upheld as no abuse of discretion. The commercial-premises-privacy point the wiki cites it for is present in the opinion's reasoning (a business's non-public interior/loading-dock area still needing consent or PC) but is supporting analysis, not the operative holding. Illustrative/persuasive use is defensible — NOT a clean CONTEXT-MISMATCH, NOT fabrication. DECOY: 'State v. Weaver, 945 S.W.2d 334' (Tex. Crim. App. 1998) is a different case.

court: U.S. Court of Appeals, Tenth Circuit
context_note: REFUTES the fabrication/'invented-framework' suspicion. Real and correctly stated: a Triple-I criminal-history check during a speeding stop is a negligibly-burdensome officer-safety inquiry within the stop's mission under Rodriguez v. United States, so it did not unlawfully prolong the stop; denial of suppression affirmed. Holding matches the wiki's Traffic Stops text exactly. Directly verified.

court: U.S. Court of Appeals, Fourth Circuit
context_note: REFUTES the fabrication/'invented-framework' suspicion. Real and correctly stated: although the simple loss of a phone does not forfeit REP, Small deliberately discarded his phone during flight (NSA-gate crash near Fort Meade, fleeing on foot, tossing personal items), which the 4th Cir. held a voluntary abandonment; he lost REP in the device and its digital contents; suppression denial affirmed. Holding matches the wiki's Abandonment text. Directly verified.

court: U.S. Court of Appeals, Second Circuit
context_note: REFUTES the fabrication/'invented-framework' suspicion. Real and correctly stated: an unlicensed driver operating a rental car without the rental company's permission is, like a car thief, unlawfully in possession and has no REP — so no standing — even though the authorized renter (his girlfriend) let him drive; reads Byrd's lawful-possession requirement narrowly and expressly declined to decide whether an unauthorized-but-licensed driver alone would have standing. Holding matches the wiki's Standing text exactly. Directly verified.

court: U.S. Court of Appeals, First Circuit (en banc)
context_note: REFUTES the 'backwards-holding' fabrication scar — the CURRENT wiki text reflects the CORRECTED holding and is accurate. Real: the en banc First Circuit divided 3-3 on whether sustained warrantless pole-camera surveillance of a home's curtilage is a 4A search (Carpenter mosaic vs. no search), but UNANIMOUSLY reversed the district court's suppression order and admitted the ~8 months of pole-camera evidence under the Davis good-faith exception (reliance on then-binding circuit precedent, Bucci). Cert. denied May 22, 2023. No backwards holding present in current text. Directly verified.
